review_note: Infinite product of three-term abelian-group complexes has homology equal to the product of individual homology groups, by exactness of products. Matched against the pinned original theorem text in the Stage A source packet; did not open proof/remark text. Preliminary decision only.
statement:
Let $I$ be a set. For $i \in I$ let $L_i \to M_i \to N_i$ be a complex
of abelian groups. Let $H_i = \Ker(M_i \to N_i)/\Im(L_i \to M_i)$
be the cohomology. Then
$$
\prod L_i \to \prod M_i \to \prod N_i
$$
is a complex of abelian groups with homology $\prod H_i$.
hypotheses: Let $(L_i\to M_i\to N_i)_{i\in I}$ be set-indexed complexes of abelian groups and let $H_i=\ker(M_i\to N_i)/\operatorname{im}(L_i\to M_i)$.
conclusions: The product sequence is a complex with middle cohomology naturally isomorphic to $\prod_iH_i$.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-product-abelian-groups-exact}
Let $I$ be a set. For $i \in I$ let $L_i \to M_i \to N_i$ be a complex
of abelian groups. Let $H_i = \Ker(M_i \to N_i)/\Im(L_i \to M_i)$
be the cohomology. Then
$$
\prod L_i \to \prod M_i \to \prod N_i
$$
is a complex of abelian groups with homology $\prod H_i$.
